text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Over-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset with Micro-USB and 3.5 Audio Cable - Black These over the ear Bluetooth earphones are just over the ear Bluetooth ear phones. They are not noise cancelling, so if that is what you want then you'd better pass on by. These are a basic Bluetooth Wireless Headphones.

Unboxing you get the headphones, and two different cords. One cord to charge the headphones (USB plug) and one cord to use the headphones outside of Bluetooth mode. I plugged them in my laptop overnight to charge it up and then took them to work to see how they would do. At work, I found out they do not cancel noise. I could still hear every single conversation around me whether music was playing or not. To drown out conversation, I would have to turn the sound way up, but I'd rather save my hearing. However, my purposes it's ok. I really just wanted the overhead head phones to indicate to people that I'm working. For some reason, earbuds just don't communicate that I'm busy. I had to use the audio cord in my mp3 (from a famous manufacturer) because I have a first generation unit that doesn't have Bluetooth ability. I felt that earbuds vs. these were no different. I decided to start with something bass inducing, so started with early 00's Hip Hop. The bass on my earbuds is better. I then worked my thru my R&B & Alternative lists, and then finally something with high pitched tones (strings) like Irish Folk. I felt that my earbuds had slightly better sound quality. However, I did not feel like was missing out on much.

Next, I brought them home and tested them out with my laptop in Bluetooth mode. Set-up was easy. My laptop has a Bluetooth icon and I just asked it to look for Bluetooth devices. After a few seconds, AmazonBasics Bluetooth Headphones popped-up. I told it to connect and then pumped up the jamz (it's always with a z). After a couple hours, I got up to adjust the thermostat on the A/C. I walked from the dining room thru the living room and into the foyer. I realized as I was walking back I still had the headphones on! I completely forgot! So, that means they are comfortable. A little heavy, but I obviously got used to it.

Finally, I tested them with my tablet (again a well-known brand) and I was not able to connect to it. I then tried to reconnect to my laptop and the laptop did not reconnect. The instructions are no good in troubleshooting this issue. So, now I have to connect via the cable all the time, which defeats the purpose. I can use the earbuds that I've been using. Plus, my laptop stopped producing sound altogether. Additionally, when they are playing everyone can hear what you listening to, so they will not be that helpful. If my son is standing next to me or sitting at the table with me, he can hear every word from my HipHop mix. Not ideal. Speaking of HipHop, another downside is that these, unlike a well-known brand with the name of a rapper/producer attached to them, do not fold up. So, they are big and bulky in your bag when you are carrying them around. I'm also afraid that something in my purse or mini backpack is going to do something to them. I also have to make sure I'm carrying a big purse to transport these around.

Pros:
-Wireless! (Don't disconnect from the device once you get it connected you'll never get it back.)
-Comfortable on the ears
-Easy set-up

Cons:
-Not Noise Cancelling
-Sound Quality could be better
-Heavy
-Does not fold up (Bulky to carry around)
-Must use the cable if you disconnect from a device. It will not reconnect.

UPDATE: The fix to my connection issue was on Pg. 6 of the instructions, but that's not how I connected the first time. Now, that I am reconnected to my laptop, the sound is like being underwater and goes in and out. So, it's tricky and sometimes you will have a set of wireless headphones, and sometimes you won't.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Over-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset with Micro-USB and 3.5 Audio Cable - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Joymax 4MP Ultra HD Webcam with Microphone - 360-Degree Rotating Computer Camera for Work at Home Jobs - High Definition Web Cam for PC Laptop - Live Streaming Desktop Camera with Noise Cancellation A lot of these cheap webcams use very small sensors and rely on super wide optics to see the room. They also tend to overstate their resolving power, claiming to send a 1080 sized image that looks more like an upscaled 480. I'm happy to say this is a degree better than those!
The sensor is still small, as expected, but the optics aren't super wide to the point that edges distort. In fact, it seems pretty rectilinear (straight lines stay relatively straight in the background). The resolution seems decent as well. I'm not sure if it's actually resolved a full HD image like it claims, but it is definitely more resolution than a lot of the cheaper webcams I've tried. It looks pretty good and I'd argue that any live web call, skype, zoom, etc, will look perfectly fine with this camera and play at whatever resolution that protocol is capable of clearly.
The thing that sorta disappointed me, however, was the "ring light" built in. I mean, I have a REAL ring light so I get what that should do, but this sorta does... nothing. It doesn't create soft shadows or a circular catch light in my eyes- in fact, it's very hard to discern the difference between capture with the light on versus off. In a dark room, it can add a bit of illumination to the subject to make you a little easier to see, but it really isn't all that bright and under normal lighting conditions in my office, it makes zero difference at all. It also seems to get kind of warm as long as it is plugged in, even if not currently active, so I'm going to be in the habit of disconnecting it when not using, and only plugging it in when I need to make a video call at my desk.
For what it is, it is definitely a better webcam than most of the cheap ones, but it definitely is not perfect!
text_fidelity_b: Joymax 4MP Ultra HD Webcam with Microphone - 360-Degree Rotating Computer Camera for Work at Home Jobs - High Definition Web Cam for PC Laptop - Live Streaming Desktop Camera with Noise Cancellation

This is NOT the speaker that you simply grab and throw in the bag and go. This speaker is rather large and surprisingly VERY heavy.

The sound quality is nice but the bass is only ok in my opinion. I have another speaker which is made by Amazon that cost about $50 that has the exact same sound quality. It is loud but as with this bass, ive heard others that are louder and cost much less.

I will start with the app that the instructions tell you that you need to download. It states that it is for updates, but all I saw is that it is used for is linking multiple speakers together.

I wanted this speaker because we spend alot of time out by the pool and at the river during the summer. I knew that I wanted something that was water proof for both of those settings so I was happy to give this one a try. As I mentioned before, this sucker is HEAVY so while it may be water proof, if you were to drop in the river at any point it would go straight to the bottom never to be seen again, so it wouldn't really matter how water proof it is. For the pool and sitting stationary, it would be perfect.

One use that I can see us using this speaker would be for travel baseball games. It is loud enough that you would be able to hear it from a distance.

As I said earlier... some will love this speaker and think that it is absolutely worth it. Others will not. This speaker will strictly come down to personal opinion. For instance, other than the weight, I love this speaker. My spouse thinks that his $50 is much better.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wireless All-In-One Media Keyboard,Black - Wireless Keyboard with Track Pad. USB Wireless Receiver. Spill Resistant Design. 2AAA Batteries Included. Most people purchase this wireless keyboard to use at home with their TV or other media setup. I actually purchased it to use at work as a more ergonomic option. No, this is not billed as an ergonomic keyboard, but the main issue I was having was reaching for the mouse, so I wanted something with a built-in trackpad. Surprisingly, there are VERY FEW options available, particularly within a reasonable price range (<50) and offered by a name brand company.

Prior to purchasing this keyboard, I tried another which featured the trackpad front and center ([[ASIN:B004KN7PZG Gear Head USB Smart Touch II Touchpad Keyboard]]). Unfortunately, that product was way too glitchy, and the size was not ideal. I thought that the center trackpad would work well given that I'm used to using one on my laptop at home (a [[ASIN:B00IPQXZ62 Dell XPS Convertible 2 in 1]], which has a near-ideal keyboard), but that did not seem to be the case. When I began looking for keyboards with a built-in trackpad on the side, this one by Microsoft seemed to be the only viable option, although I wasn't looking for wireless.

I did like that that the keyboard is Microsoft, and I like the clean look and design. Compared to the prior keyboard that I tried, this one definitely has a more comfortable feel. Although it is small, there is adequate spacing around the keys, something the prior keyboard lacked. There is no number pad--the trackpad replaces this--but as I never used this anyway, this is no loss for me. All of the keys are a nice size, including the shift keys (these are sometimes skimped upon). Unfortunately, there is no "End" key--I knew that upon purchasing, but I still miss it. What I did NOT realize is that in order to access the Function keys, you actually have to HOLD DOWN the "FN" button. This is a bit of a pain for me, as I use Refresh (F5) constantly, so this is now a 2-handed operation. This keyboard is also missing any kind of indicator for CAPS LOCK.

The trackpad is okay. I still have my mouse plugged in, and unfortunately, I find myself using it too often, as the trackpad is not completely reliable. It does accept multi-finger scrolling gestures, which is nice, and it does pretty well with simple up-down navigation; however, I have found that side-to-side is much more uneven. I do like that there is a left-hand click button on the right side of the keyboard, and I have made use of this at times. But I've also found that sometimes my palm randoming activates the trackpad when I am typing, causing the cursor to flip to a new spot on screen, which is annoying. So, at best, this has been just average.

This keyboard includes other features that I don't use--e.g., a volume control, a separate mute button (are both necessary?), home and other "hot" keys, etc. I'm assuming that these extras would be more beneficial to someone using the keyboard in a home media setting. For my needs, this keyboard has been okay. The layout is decent, although it could have been much, much better with a few minor changes. Depending on how you plan to use it, I would recommend it with reservations.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless All-In-One Media Keyboard,Black - Wireless Keyboard with Track Pad. USB Wireless Receiver. Spill Resistant Design. 2AAA Batteries Included.

.
Original Review - I bought this 24" Vizio because it was the only one in it's size that has a dedicated headphone jack. It connected to WI-fi without a problem and I signed into Netflix. I noticed right away that the opening screen was washed out and dull. I tried several different movies and shows and they all looked washed out. After 10 minutes of fiddling with all of the image controls, the image was improved but was still poor compared to our 10 year old LG in the other room. To save log-in time, I connected an already logged-in Roku to the HDMI input on the TV.
As soon as I selected the Roku HDMI input the on-screen image dramatically improved. Checking the same Netflix movies and shows as before, it was always much brighter and more vibrant than when using built-in streaming. Images on other services like Hulu were also quite watchable.
I was going to return the set until I hooked up the Roku. With the improved image coming from the HDMI input, my wife and I will give it a week's trial.
I would strongly not recommend this set if you intend to use its internal ("smart") capability. If you're going to use an external Roku, Chromcast, Apple TV, or similar HDMI-connected box, it's worth a try considering the price and inputs and outputs. The audio quality is adequate. Neither bad nor great.

Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue I was so excited to receive these headphones and give them a go. I’ve spent right at a week with them and this is what I’ve found.

There are little to no instructions regarding these headphones and I had to research the app that has to be downloaded and go to the Razer website to begin using. Once I had everything set up, it was easy. I would have rather had a semblance of instruction than the wild packaging. The headphones were easy to pair to my phone and the sound is crystal clear. I was impressed with the noise cancelation especially. As an audiophile, I am very, very critical of sound and what is missing with these headphones is any kind of upper volume range or bass. For the price, I would have expected better in that department.

The strongest plus to these headphones is the clarity of the music. Even with the lower volume and the lack of bass, the music is sharp and clear - something I have found gets lost with other brands. The noise cancellation is also a strength above others.

Overall, I would recommend if you’re not searching for heavily bassed or volumed headphones.

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS N53SM-ES72 15.6-Inch Laptop (Silver Aluminum) I'll update later. First thing I did was toy with it a little to make sure it worked, then I installed Ubuntu 12.04. THEN I found out that there are not reliable drivers for using the optimus feature in linux. I went with this laptop so that I can play one game in particular. After spending HOURS tweeking, installing and experimenting, I'm at the point where I can say, if you plan on using this machine for linux AND gaming, either walk on by, or plan on dual booting or running a virtual machine (which one I've not decided I'll do yet). I THINK if there was the ability in the BIOS to turn off the intel graphics card in favor of only using the nvidia, that might be helpful.
The design is nice, it's fast and it may be heavy by today's standards, but compared to the Dell d810 I'm replacing, this is light.
The price point is, as stated by many before, excellent.

I take away the star for the simple fact that it's FAR too late in the game for nvidia to not have appropriate drivers to support this card fully in linux.

I do NOT want to run windows 7, but it looks like I'll be recovering it and spending hours decrapifying.

Update: May, 14, 2012
I've now had the laptop running a dual boot of Ubuntu 12.04 and Windows 7. I initially tried to just run Ubuntu and gave up on the driver debacle - fail for nvidia - and went back to reinstall. Major advice, when you get this machine, BOOT IT AND MAKE THE RECOVERY DVD SET!!! It took 4 DVDs and actually a little while, but it was the best move. When I went to recover W7, it did not properly use the recovery partition. The DVDs rebuild the partition (and destroy everything else in the process) back to factory. That was ok for me, I was testing and didn't lose anything worth saving.

Boot is fast. Ubuntu shuts down super fast, so the time to switch isn't bad. I play my game (Lord of the Rings Online - mostly set as ultra settings) quit and reboot into linux so I can enjoy my daily computing experience.

The plus other mention is the full HD experience. My previous laptop did 1900x100. I miss the vertical resolution, but am getting used to only having 1080. The screen is great. I do not understand why people like the glossy/glare screens. I hate them. This is pretty matte.

Temperature-wise it runs lap-top ok. The left side vent blows warm/hot air, which was actually nice on my hand in the cold basement during gaming (I'm a lefty - using a mouse).

I'm getting used to the keyboard. I often find it misses some of my key strokes, but I might just need to MEAN them a little more, as I tend to type with a softer touch. This makes the typing experience a little louder than I prefer, but my wife doesn't complain, so it can't be that bad.

I'm a tad less fond of the USB placement. They are toward the front of the sides, which means the USB plugs are close to all my business. If I had the RJ45 connected as well, it would be more annoying wires up close and personal.

As or resources, it feels perfectly adequate for my needs. This weekend I was running about 60 firefox tabs, 10 chrome tabs, a handful of libre office documents, Redblade 3.5 (D&D character generator) running twice via wine, about 15 20-50MB PDFs, ktorrent, and a few other things here and there concurrently without a hiccup. Eventually, maybe I'll upgrade to more ram, but I cannot currently see any reason for it. I also can't see a particular reason to plunk down for a SSD. I imagine the power saving would be nice. I do get only around 2-2.5 hours of regular use off power, but since this is a desktop replacement, that's less of an issue. If it was less than 1.5 hrs, I'd be troubled.

The quickboot option boots into an OS experience for basic web browsing, some games, IM... I suppose the most basic of what a netbook would be for. In a pinch, it's FAST to get into and connects to wifi quickly. Navigating is funky, but it's not meant for full on use - otherwise you blew $900 on a pretty low end experience.

I still deduct the star almost exclusively for the video drivers issue and the inability to select which video to use in the BIOS. If I could run from the nvidia, I believe there wouldn't be the issues with driver support in linux, as the GPU is supported - it's the switching that's picky.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS N53SM-ES72 15.6-Inch Laptop (Silver Aluminum)

Digital Camera Auto Focus 2.7K 48MP Digital Point and Shoot Camera with 32GB Memory Card,16X Zoom, Time Lapse Vlogging Camera Digital Cameras for 8-15 Years Kids Teenagers Students Boys Girls This is a great little camera. It takes surprisingly good pictures. I guess I wasn't expecting much for a kids camera. It is pretty easy to operate. All the pictures in my review were taken on my recent visit to Colorado. As you can see, it handled a variety of shots with aplomb. The wildflowers was a closeup, the two landscapes were long shots with varying light conditions. The stained glass shot is the ceiling on the Broadmore Hotel in Colorado Springs. Everything came out clear and beautiful. I am not very steady when I hold a camera, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that most of my shots aren't fuzzy or blurred from my wobbly camera holding.

The only reason I didn't give this camera a top rating is because of the viewfinder. There isn't one, and the view screen is stationary. There is no way to rotate it or adjust it so that you can see what you are trying to shoot from any angle that you might hold it at. That made getting a good shot very challenging. The wildflower shot, for instance, was taken completely blind. I could not see the view screen at all. That would have meant crawling on the ground to see the screen. I can't get on the ground (mobility issues). I had to just gold the camera in front of the flowers and snap the picture, hoping for the best. The other issue is that, because you can't adjust the view screen, lighting conditions often make the screen unseeable, even if you are looking straight at it. The second landscape photo (the one on the right) was impossible to see what I was shooting at, even though I was looking directly at the screen. The lighting prevented me from being able to see the screen. Luckily, I got a good shot anyway, but I really don't like shooting blind.

So, overall, I recommend this camera. It is a good beginning camera. Very basic, takes good photos. It's just hard to use in some circumstances.
text_fidelity_b: Digital Camera Auto Focus 2.7K 48MP Digital Point and Shoot Camera with 32GB Memory Card,16X Zoom, Time Lapse Vlogging Camera Digital Cameras for 8-15 Years Kids Teenagers Students Boys Girls

Elgood Tabletop Vacuum Cleaner with Cleaning Brush,Eraser dust Vacuum USB Charging,Best Desk Vacuum No Dead Angle Cleaning(Green) Like many single guys I have various pockets of dust scattered around my place. My desk, behind the computer towers and monitors where all the cords are piled up is one of the worst. So a handheld vacuum to clean all those nooks and crannies sounded like a good idea. Sadly, this is not the portable vacuum that I am looking for.

A few design flaws were obvious as soon as I took this out of the box and started charging it. There is no stand or holder for the vacuum so it has to sit directly on the brushes you've just been cleaning with. The light indicating when the vacuum is charging/fully charged is pinhole size, barely visible from any distance. So I had to go pick it up and squint at the light to see if it was charged up. The little brush for cleaning the inside of the vacuum is one more tiny thing to keep track of and is easily lost.

Even more flaws became obvious as soon as I tried to use the vacuum. With the nozzle on I tried to clean the back of my desk where all the computer wires are. The nozzle immediately jammed up on hair and dust balls. That area is still as dusty now as it was before I tried to vacuum it. Next I tried cleaning some flat surfaces. The brushes pushed the dust back and forth while barely vacuuming any of it up. I put my hand across the bottom of the brushes and could not feel any suction at all. When I put my finger right into the center hole that the dust was supposed to be scooped up into, I could barely feel a tiny amount of suction. I still very much like the idea of a handheld vacuum but I very much do not like this one and cannot recommend it to anyone.
text_fidelity_b: Elgood Tabletop Vacuum Cleaner with Cleaning Brush,Eraser dust Vacuum USB Charging,Best Desk Vacuum No Dead Angle Cleaning(Green)

LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports I received this as a free review sample and it was sorely needed because the internal fan in my ThinkPad T61 finally died. Note: if you are looking at this as a cure know that many laptops report a fan failure then shut down. In the case of mine, I found that I could press the On/Off button briefly when that happened and it would power back up and boot Windows.

This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. So far it has worked well and I have had no premature shutdowns (although I still have to go through the On/Off button sequence every time I power the ThinkPad up.)

Do be aware that this fan array will interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved.

Also, this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two.

If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports

Besides the added comfort, another advantage of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is that it requires less space than a traditional mouse. Because this mouse is stationary and doesn't need to be dragged across a desk or other surface, it can fit into many small spaces. You don't need to make room to drag it, so it can be placed in tight quarters. This is great for those who work in offices with limited desk space.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse offers four buttons to use for clicking. The large tabs on each side of the mouse are used for the usual right and left click functions and then there are two smaller tabs right above each of the larger tabs that are used for various functions. These two small tabs can be programmed to perform several things, and many will likely program them to scroll since this Logitech mouse doesn't have a scroll wheel. But the tabs can be programmed for other things, too. Since I don't necessarily need to scroll, my small tabs have been programmed as browser back and forward buttons. This makes life a little easier because I no longer need to move my mouse to the top of my screen and click the forward and backward arrows in the upper left corner. I just click my small left tab to go back and my small right tab to go forward.

The Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse is a marked improvement compared to the standard mouse, but I admit that it does take some getting used to. Having used a traditional mouse for most of my computer- using years, I had grown accustomed to sliding my mouse across the desk surface. Thus, when I started to use the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse, I kept sliding it around on my desk also, even though I knew this mouse didn't need to be dragged. It took some time to break this habit. It also took time to get used to the sensitivity of the trackball. The slightest movement sends your pointer flying and when I first started to use this mouse, I would continually underestimate the precision of the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse. My movements of the trackball were far too extreme. The pointer would soar across my computer screen, even though I would swear I wasn't moving the trackball very much. It is a very sensitive device that almost seems too loose at first because it moves so freely and with such little effort.

Compared to a traditional mouse, the Logitech Trackball Marble Mouse has many great things to offer and it is a mouse I am happy I took the time to try. It is superior to the traditional model in most areas, reducing pain and strain and offering greater accuracy and an easy grip. It does take time to get used to, but it is worth it in the long run and even those who initially resist the change will be happy, in due time, that they made the switch to Logitech.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Optical Trackball Marble Mouse

iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair) My old G930 ear pads were flaking like crazy after several years of daily, all-day use, and I was hesitant to buy these at first because several people said they were too small. But I figured it's only $5, so it's worth a shot.

They arrived this morning and all I can think of is that whoever thought these were too tight or too small wasn't putting them on correctly. Maybe they thought they were just push-on instead of realizing that they have a flap (just like the ones that come with the headset) that needs to be lifted to go over the plastic part of the earpiece. That's what actually holds these things in place, people - otherwise they'd just fall off! Or maybe people aren't actually matching up the shape correctly. Either way - if you install them CORRECTLY, they fit perfectly.

These things are the correct size and I took some photos to compare the old Logitech-made pads with these. I also measured separately and they are the exact same size. If you take the time to look at how the original ear pads come off, you'll know exactly how to put these replacements on, and it'll take you all of about 10-15 seconds per ear pad.

These are virtually indistinguishable from the originals. I put these on and at first they seemed a little firmer than the original ear pads. However, I actually have a total of three G930 headsets (different purposes), so I was able to compare the feel of these ear pads to the original ear pads on one of the lesser-used, newer headsets. Again, pretty much identical - I guess they just get softer with use. Still, they are very comfortable even in their brand-new state, and I'm happy not to finish the day with black flakes on the sides of my face again.

PHOTOS:
I have three photos, two that are just comparing the back and front of the old pad to the replacement pad (and showing where the flap is that some people are apparently missing). The third photo is just showing the headset with one pad replaced so you can actually see that it looks pretty much the same as the original when installed correctly on the headset.

text_fidelity_a:
OHDERII TV Projector I got excited to see one of these small portable LED style ones that actually had a decent native resolution (most of them can accept 1080p, but are in reality only 800x600 resolution, or sometimes worse... 640x480!). This one is actually capable of displaying 720p of real dot resolution, which should make it at least as sharp as my Viewsonic and other traditional HD projectors. Ok, perhaps I'm spoiled, but I'm comparing this to our Viewsonic 720p projector that, to be fair cost me 3-4x as much.
And for the most part, it DOES work, however there are some caveats to its use. First of all, it doesn't seem as sharp as my 720p projector, even though it should have the requisite amount of dots. It's OK, its definitely better than the cheap 600p projectors, but something just isn't quite there when comparing side by side. It also doesn't get all that bright, but I suppose that's expected from the LED tech being used. You'll need black out shades or use it only during the night. Then there's the color- it isn't great. It works, but it has a cheap color reproduction that looks kind of flat and lifeless. Dark scenes sort of all blend together and become nearly impossible to see. It lacks the vibrancy of even an inexpensive television from decades ago. It gets the job done, but hardly the "theater experience" if you've been waiting to see that latest action/vfx film the way it was intended. It will look better on your TV at home, the only thing this has going for it is the large projection experience. For example, if you just want to give your kids a backyard movie night and don't care that the color and detail won't be as great as your indoor system, it will do the job on the cheap. I personally would not give up my mid-range projector for this one.
One thing that I found particularly annoying is that rather than the optical zoom and focus dials found on usual projectors, there is only a focus and tilt dial. No zoom. That means you have to physically move the projector closer or further to get it to reach the correct size you are shooting for. That actually got in the way of using it in a couple of specific places my other projectors can be used at optimal sizes.
That's not to say it gets everything wrong- I DO like that it is small and light and can even be turned on it's back to aim at the ceiling. That's something my big projector can't do, due to the airflow and cable management sticking out the rear. It also has a standard 1/4" 20 threaded tripod mounting point, so you can place this onto a tripod and get maximum mounting freedom. That will come in handy as I've always wanted to watch a movie in bed on the ceiling. But otherwise, don't think this projector will be as good as the other mid-rangers out there. This is still very much a low end projector. You'll have to spend at least 2-3x as much to get a decent home theater style experience, and much more if you want a high end one that will handle FHD/4k to get the real deal. This is more of a specialty use item.
text_fidelity_b: OHDERII TV Projector

WDX Grommet Hole in Desk USB 3.0 3 Port Hub BC 1.2 USB Charger with 3.5mm Audio Mic Phone Jack, 5V/2A Power Adapter for iPhone/Smart Phones(AC Power Supply Included) A couple of weeks ago I got a monitor stand to use on my desk. It had a large circular hole on the back of the monitor shelf along with a plastic cover for the hole. Apparently the idea was to give a discreet place to run the monitor's plug through. That seemed like a silly waste to me as you could just run the plug off the back of the stand with much less hassle. So the idea of this product, using that hole for a charger with some extra USB connections, seemed like a good idea to me. A real caveat though is that there are several essential details to pay attention to in using this item.

The first essential detail is to pay attention to the size of the hole you are going to use this on and the size of this product. Apparently those holes are not a standard size and some folks have had issues using this item because of that. Handyman types who have the tools to enlarge a grommet hole have an advantage here but it would behoove everyone to make sure this product will fit what they need.

The second detail to notice is that this device only works with USB 3.0 devices. The 2.0 ones won't work. My desktop computer has both 2.0 and 3.0 USB plugs. You can plug any device into any of those slots and it will work although the speed may vary. A 2.0 device plugged into a 3.0 slot will run but at 2.0 speeds. With this product, the 2.0 devices won't work at all.

The final detail to watch out for may be the most important one. Several people who have plugged the charger into their computer have reported difficulties it's created with their machines. So if you want to do that, pay very close attention the first time you try it to avoid any problems.
text_fidelity_b: WDX Grommet Hole in Desk USB 3.0 3 Port Hub BC 1.2 USB Charger with 3.5mm Audio Mic Phone Jack, 5V/2A Power Adapter for iPhone/Smart Phones(AC Power Supply Included)

It's a good way of keeping your machine safe from malware attacks. No need to purchase and renew antiviral software. The screen is clear and bright, and the keyboard works really nicely. The sound from these is much better than the sound on my much more expensive laptop. Overall, the size and functionality of the Chromebook is much better than my new Windows 8.1 laptop.

My kids were able to get started immediately with minimal help from me to download some apps they like, get their e-mails set up and started using these Chromebooks immediately. I personally am not nuts about having only Google Chrome as my internet browser, thus I don't own my own Chromebook, but for my kids purposes (mainly games and schoolwork) the Chromebooks work out great. I really like how easy and smoothly they work. They are faster than my laptop and I do find that appealing, but I like being able to use a DVD drive and to be able to download what software I might want from the internet.

Printing is possible from the cloud and set up to do that is not difficult. Everything is easy........almost too easy. You can't store any data on the computer itself, only in the cloud. But, I'm not worried about any personal information being accessed by nefarious types because there's really nothing to access.

We've had these Chromebooks since Christmas and they are still working fine with no problems whatsoever.

UPDATE: 2.28.15 - My daughter brought it to my attention that these chromebooks do not have a "delete" key. Interesting.

text_fidelity_a:
XPPen Deco Pro Small Graphics Drawing Tablet Ultrathin Digital Pen Tablet with Tilt Function Double Wheel and 8 Shortcut Keys 8192 Levels Pressure 9x5 Inch Working Area THE GOOD:
--------------
* High quality premium build.
* Direct usb-c connection, or Bluetooth connection.
* There is no delay with Bluetooth connection. My drawings are instantaneous. If there are any delays, it is imperceptible to my eyes.
* 8 shortcut keys, and roller wheel. Once you use this tablet, you'll never use another writing tablet without these shortcuts. They are so convenient.
* Roller wheel can be assigned as a zoom in/out function, a scroller, change brush size, or rotate images. I have mine set to change brush size. This is so much more convenient than going to the upper left menu in photoshop to change brush size. Plus, at default from the factory, the 8th shortcut key is programmed for you to access and change the roller functions quickly. So even though I have my roller set to change brush size, if I hit the 8th key, I get a pop-up menu of my choices again.
* Top of the roller wheel is a touch pad, so you can assign it as a mouse.
* Pen is housed in a cylinder with storage on both ends. On one end is the actual pen, and on the other end is storage for the Bluetooth usb dongle, and 10 replacement pen nibs/tips.
* As is, the idea is you write with your right hand, and your left hand controls the wheel and shortcut keys. What if you're left handed? In the XP-Pen software, you can flip the layout 180, this will allow you to flip the tablet so the roller and shortcut keys are on the right. You must set this in the program. If you don't, and you flip the tablet, everything will just move in reverse.

THE BAD:
-----------
* We will all have a different experience because we all use different apps and programs. I use Photoshop CS6 and the roller was quirky. None of the roller functions worked. So I switched programs and used Windows Paint, and everything worked fine. When I went back to CS6, the roller started working. As if it learned something from the Paint program. LOL! I uploaded a bunch of screenshots of the software so you can see what setting and features are available.

I will rate this 4-Stars for now. I'm pretty sure it's the tablet that's quirky with CS6, and not user error. But I'll be using this a lot in the next few weeks, and I'll bump this to 5-Stars should I learn that it was user error. But so far, I don't think I'm doing anything wrong, the roller is just really quirky in CS6.
text_fidelity_b: XPPen Deco Pro Small Graphics Drawing Tablet Ultrathin Digital Pen Tablet with Tilt Function Double Wheel and 8 Shortcut Keys 8192 Levels Pressure 9x5 Inch Working Area

text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2) Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2)

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor This little device does a lot.
While it is sort of a smart watch, it sort of isn't, too. But what it does, it does well.

The good:
- Excellent selection of watch faces, including cute, clever, big, pretty, etc. You can change your face every day to match your clothes if you want.
- If I understand correctly, you can use it with other services, like Spark People.
- measures pulse, steps, miles. Tracks exercise on demand.
- motivates in numerous ways. Reminders to stand up, encouragement to finish your goal steps for the hour, challenges, even "travel" challenges that are longer term.
- large userbase. You can network with more of your friends on Fitbit than on any other fitness watch.
- big face without losing attractiveness
- large variety of replacement bands available from third parties, some very pretty.
- Can be used with many other fitness applications.
- Detects sleep surprisingly accurately
- Lots of settings options
- A decent number of apps available
- Handles the shower well
- If you never have to take it off except to charge, it's harder to lose it.
- Charges very quickly
- The charger is an awesome design and easy to use
- You can always have your alarms with you so you never miss them.

The irritating
- All changes have to be made through the app.
- If you don't sync often enough, it loses your data
- Sync can take a long time.
- The battery life is considerably shorter than I expected. It's about 2 1/2 days if I have constant sync turned off.
- Don't even bother with constant sync unless you're willing to take it off to charge a lot.
- All the music apps are paid

All in all, though, the pros are big and the cons are small. Enough that it still warrants a 5 star review.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor

The best feature for me is the enhanced grip. Sweaty palms have led to a couple of close calls in the past. I used the 40D with armor today in the 90 degree heat, and the camera felt far, far more secure in my hands. Much better gripabilty (if that is a word). I imagine it would also help with gripping the camera when it's very cold and fingers get stiff. Will have to wait several months before I can find that out for sure.

If you use your 40D/50D outdoors, this is an excellent product to have.

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter This seemed to be the perfect solution to a problem I was having with obtaining Internet access in my basement. The router is located on the upper floor of the house and, while access is fine in every room above ground, access in the basement has been minimal at best.

Installation was very straightforward - just plug one adapter into the router, the other into the wall socket, and plug in whatever device needs access into one of the three plugs located on the wall socket device.

Overall it works pretty well, but is highly sensitive to noise or heavy draws on the power line. For example, I have a dehumidifier in the basement. When that kicks on, I lose the connection. Sometimes it is regained all by itself, but most of the time I have to either reboot (or power cycle) the device that is plugged in, or unplug and then re-plug the adapter. I tried moving the dehumidifier to a different circuit than the one used by the powerline adapter, and also tried plugging the dehumidifier into a surge protector - no difference. So, I make sure the dehumidifier is off before I use any Internet device.

I've had the same issue with other appliances such as certain vacuums - turn them on, and the connection is lost. There have been no problems with appliances operating in other areas of the house, such as the microwave, laser printers, etc. Just happens when you use the appliance in the same room as the powerline adapter.

But, other than these powerline induced interruptions, the device works well. Speedy connection - can't tell any difference between this and any other WiFi connected device. Well worth taking a look at if you have some WiFi dead zones in your house. Just keep an eye out for someone who is about to use a vacuum when you're at a critical spot in the movie you're streaming!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation) The Flip is a pint-sized camcorder with a surprising feature set given its compactness. Though is it not a full-featured camcorder and I would not recommend it for serious recording (special events or production material), it is excellent for on-the-go shots and for spontaneous recording when opportunities present themselves.

The Flip is small - a little smaller than an ice cream sandwich. It may be little, but there's tremendous convenience in being able to drop your camcorder in your shirt pocket or your purse and have it at the ready. This compact size holds everything you need to start recording - batteries, flash RAM and all. Without tapes or DVD media on which to record, there's little reason for this device to be any bigger.

It is a solid little thing and feels durable. That doesn't mean it would do well if dropped or stepped on, but it likely will be ok if jostled a little.

Recording is simple. No, I should be more clear - recording with the Flip is trivial. There is no real science to using it: turn it on, point and press record. Press the record button again to stop recording. Even technological novices, or people afraid of electronics will have no trouble using the Flip to record. Playing back is equally simple - once the recording is finished, press the Play button.

There are + and - buttons, used for Zoom. The Flip doesn't have a particularly capable zoom, so shooting from a distance will not yield especially great results.

I tested this camcorder in my basement on a bright, sunny day, and I wandered about recording and chattering to myself. When I played back what I had recorded, I made a pleasant discovery - it does some light balancing and deals with changes in light levels so that the video is still clear. The sound is also good, better than I expected. When I walked down a dark hallway and into an unlit room, it had tried very hard to accommodate for the lack of light but it was unable to completely overcome the darkness. As there is no light on the camcorder to come on when it is dark, this is understandable, but it did surprisingly well in spite of that.

I attached the Flip to my computer to pull the video to my hard drive. FlipShare installed itself and started up, seeing the video I had made. It allowed me to pull it over and even gave me the option to delete it from the camera. Once finished, I was able to play the video through FlipShare. Instead, I decided to hunt it down and use a different application to play it.

I found the file and tried to open it with Windows Media Player. I got audio, but not video. When I switched to QuickTime, my video came up and filled my screen. This is the point at which I made an unfortunate discovery. Every minute move I had made while recording was now plainly obvious, as there is no anti-jitter built into the device.

The video, on a 1440x900 resolution screen, looked clear. It records at 1280x720, which is not that much smaller, so I was a little surprised. I would have expected a little pixelation, but this actually was not an issue.

There are few settings that can be adjusted on the Flip - language, date, time and recording light.

The Flip is a nice camcorder that provides tremendous convenience and fun. It is very easy to use and very compact. It is important to remember that it has some limitations which make it a less-than-ideal choice for more serious application, but if those limitations are not an issue for you then the Flip is a fun and affordable way to capture things on video.
text_fidelity_b: Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation)

However, I found that the hub would occasionally, without apparent cause, reset itself, causing the mouse and keyboard to be re-detected, flickering the keyboard backlight and triggering the beeps and chimes of the OS detected a connected device. Same occurred in two different power outlets, and multiple USB ports. It wasn't a major issue - everything was always redetected and working again within seconds, without my needing to do anything, but it was mildly annoying.

It is possible that it was one of my computers - the reason I was using it was that I was transitioning over to a new computer due to various issues, after all. Maybe the USB controller wasn't outputting a clean, consistent signal.

If you need this temporarily while transitioning over to a new system, or in a system which is isn't used that much, it should be fine. I wouldn't use it as a interface for my primary setup though.

text_fidelity_a: Logitech Harmony One Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) In the beginning, you will love this remote. But it will break. Guaranteed. We had one stop working, and Logitech replaced it. We dropped the replacement once (just from coffee table to floor, but it's fragile!) and the screen cracked. We were upset that it broke so easily but knew it was damage not covered by warranty, so we didn't submit a claim. We figured we'd just had a freak accident/bad luck, and bought a third one. One day I picked that one up and the screen was whited out. Over the next few days, black started to seep across the screen from one edge. By the time I had to send a picture of the remote to Logitech for our warranty claim, you could see cracks at the edge. That remote was never dropped. My best guess it that I set it down on the side table as though it were a remote, not a Faberge egg. Logitech refuses to honor their warranty. It's like beating your head against a wall. Lots of "I understand you must be frustrated," and no actual help. Not acceptable for a product that costs so much. Mine is not the only review that says this -- please believe it! Unless you have the money to buy a new one every 6 months (the longest that one of our three Harmony Ones has ever lasted), just don't do it.

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only I really bought a Canon DSLR (vs Nikon, or any of the mirrorless Cameras) for this lens. I needed a low distortion very wide lens for real estate videos and I also needed image stabilization and quiet focusing. I don't think there is any other lens from any manufacturer that satisfies all of those things except this one. (Sigma has the 10-20mm but no stabilization, lower optical quality, and more money! Tamaron - 10-24 - same story. And so on ).
GOOD: Excellent optical quality for the price. This lens is noticeably sharper and has less distortion at 10mm than my kit lens 18-135mm has at 18mm. Stabilization works very well. Focusing is very fast and silent. I don't hear it even with the built in mic when shooting video (on a Canon 70D). Extremely lightweight and fairly compact.

BAD: Maximum Aperture. This is NOT a fast lens. F/4.5 maximum is not that great and you lose it pretty quickly as you zoom in since the max aperture ranges from 4.5 - 5.6. You need to have some decent light to shoot with this lens. But given the lack of competition in super wide stabilized silent EF-S lenses (or any Canon mount lens) and the price of anything vaguely similar, I think it's a reasonable compromise.

Note: At this price, you can't really call it a knock, but it'd be nice if it came with the lens hood. You can get a clone lens hood for $10 or so.

ALSO: Canon has now updated their EOS Utility software for this lens.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 is STM Lens, Lens Only

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White) FM reception is flat out horrible where I live. It's like a radeo dead zone. My home theater system can pull in nothing. My stereo gets a lot of static. I listen almost exclusively online but I'd heard good things about this radio so I decided to give it a try. The reception was amazing. Perfectly clear. No static on FM at all. It sounds beautiful. The weather feed was full of static, but servicable--I ususally can't pull in the weather band at all. AM is average--neither the worse I've heard nor the best. But then, I don't expect much from AM.

It does the FM1, FM2 trick that some cars do. There is no difference. It just lets them repurpose the buttons. I find it odd, but not bad.

The only think I would have changed is how it hangs. If you don't have a shower hook (I don't) it hangs over the shower head. That tilts the entire unit forward. It should either suspend from the shower curtain rack (the strap is oriented the wrong way to do that--it would try to hand perpendicular to the curtain) or reach a better balance point. That's an issue of aesthetics, not function. I'd be worried about sitting it on the edge of the tub, as it is too likely to fall.

The one trick to remember, when sticking the antenna to the shower wall, is that suction cups don't work as well on a wet surface. Thoroughly dry the wall first, then place it. It helps will the issue of the antenna falling.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White)

LG Electronics 70UK6570 70-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2018 Model) I bought this set for 4k gaming (PS4 PRO) and 4k films. Anything else like voice integration with google assistant was just a bonus that adds to the overall purchases and very happy with it.

The 70/75 inch model the only major difference is screen panel type. 75 is direct lit and 70 is edge lit. Features pretty much the same.

Out of the box the image using home mode was basic due the fact that all 4k TVs are set to automatic light detection and shifts the image to 'energy saver' slightly dimming them. Just go into the menu settings, picture setting and shut energy saving mode off. This is how all major tvs are shipped inbox. Its not a defect item. After shutting that off, the image settings work like normal. Vivid, sports, cinema etc they also have a professional tv set up for light and dark room. In case you want to hire someone professionally.

HDR effect is simulated HDR on SD content. Also a separate setting for HDR called: HDMI DEEP COLOR in 'additional picture settings' same location. They also have an option for eye strain, if its set on, shut it off. Its used for people who have eye strain from bright sets. I would keep HDMI DEEP COLOR ON to test that your HDMI is working with the TV, it will automatically turn on when it detects a blue-ray disk player with HDR or gaming system using it. Leaving it on, lets you know if the HDMI is compatible with it. Even if you're not using something with HDR. If the HDMI cant pass the signal, it will default to black screen 'no image detected'. In that case shut it off, and get a new HDMI.

After shutting off power saving modes, the tv works perfectly. Vivid images, sharp, major detail and awesome color. Whites are super white, but wont bleed over each other. Reds are blood red and blacks are dark. Everything pops off the screen, keep in mind i'm coming from a 1rst gen 4k tv that lacked a full HDR panel (10 bit). Slow remote response and lacking features that this set has. THIS new set fixes all that.. The blue tooth remote is responsive, fast and almost no lag, feel snappy and responsive. You can also download the LG app and use it as a pointer (like a mouse pointer on a computer). Easiest way to input information like passwords, email etc vs dialing them in on the remote. It can also be used as a pointer to navigate menu settings on screen with click being enter command.

LG has an app store, but haven't had a chance to play around with it. They give out free screensavers images in 4k, fireplace, beach etc and some basic games. In the future, i'll download wallpapers since my gaming is done on the PS4. They also have free apps for TV viewing from online channels. The set comes pre installed with Hulu, Netflix (controller has Netflix button), YouTube, google pictures etc you can also download free online shows that stream for free. From what I read online, Netflix is tuned to the TV for best viewing.

The set also has an update feature for firmware (under about TV settings sections) and you can set it to auto update. Once registered with LG, can also be done from TV. It allows you to use Google Assistance with a few prompts for basic set up. To fully use LG AI thinQ voice built in, you have to get a magic remote (under $50 bucks) and will be buying one soon, since I use voice features a lot. From google assistant from your phone, you can do basics, volume up +5, shut living room TV off and a few other commands that go threw google assistant (phone or google home) . The magic remote uses more the voice feature and you dont have to say: okay google, tell LG to turn off living room TV" saves you a step and allows you to use it for suggestions and what you see in the demo videos. Remember that AI ThinQ is working with Google assistant for results. Not a gimped voice feature like first generation 4k TVs.

My games look phenomenal, brand new including 4k films. Everything seems to have gotten a new coat of paint. The HDR really makes a difference in films and games. These set use HDR10 and HLG (Hybrid log gamma). The only thing it does not do is Dolby Vision. Its a Dolby version of HDR basically. Which to me isn't a deal breaker since HDR10 is more supported in films, streams etc

TV also supports fast wireless connection (wireless AC).

I have nothing negative to say about the set. Had an HDMI/HDR error and that was due to my HDMI not being high speed aka 'premium HDMI'. If you run into a similar issue with PS4 PRO, XBOX X or Blu-ray player. Connect directly to set should fix the issue and see if its the HDMI. Sometimes, like in my case, its an older HDMI that I had going from my sound system out to the LG TV. The PS4 was high speed/premium but the 2nd connection to the TV wasn't, so the chain was broken. Supported 4k but lacked bandwidth with 4k+ HDR.

This set has all major functions
VA panel
Wide Color Gamut (WCG)
4K Ultra HD Resolution
4K Active HDR
Ultra Luminance

UPDATE: 9/10/2018

Installed a new HDMI high speed cable from sound system out to TV from receiver and it fixed the 'no signal' sign when HDR was turned on. Leave HDMI DEEP COLOR ON. (it will pop up the logo) to let you know its working and not a black screen. if you get a black screen somethings wrong with the HDMI. When HDR is working and pops up the logo, go to settings (gear icons in remote), pulls up quick menu and HDR will be highlighted, but say HDR+Standard imaging viewing etc (can be changed). If you're using vivid (my personal choice) when using HDR, set it to HDR+ Vivid. When you do this again, and the TV detects an HDR signal again, it will remember the last HDR+(picture setting) mode you used. (HDR on or OFF) each has thier own image settings.

Random info: if you have a sound system connected to the TV, when using built in TV set apps (You-tube/Hulu etc) you may have to set the receiver/sound system to TV on its remote to get audio coming from the sound system. If you use a Blu-ray players apps, or apps from a game system like PS4 Hulu etc just setting the normal connection input should push the sound like normal.
text_fidelity_b: LG Electronics 70UK6570 70-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2018 Model)

RCA Digital Amplifier for Indoor Antenna I "Cut the cord" and got rid of my satellite service recently, but did miss watching network TV. Consequently, I bought a Mohu Leaf TV antenna. It works well, but I added this amplifier to see if I could pull in more channels.

Short answer: For me, this amplifier works. It added 10 channels to my lineup. There are several caveats: The effectiveness of this amplifier will vary depending on your location and distance from a major city. (I'm about 60 miles from Denver.) My reception does vary depending on the weather, which can be maddening. On a good day, I can get a total of about 40 channels. Many of these channels (almost half) are religious, Spanish and shopping channels that I don't really watch.

Without the amplifier, I get about 30 channels. I have found that moving my Mohu Leaf around on the wall will improve my reception for certain channels. The important thing is to experiment to see what works for you. Check out the excellent resources online for working with an indoor TV antenna. And think of all the money you are saving!

I know compromises sometimes need to be made for a small form factor, but this is really a deal-breaker for me, so I'm returning. I also found the touchpad precision to be below average even after tinkering with the Windows mouse settings. Ehhhhh.

Well, I reserve the "right" to return for refund a product that isn't the same as what's in the pictures.

So in other words you might receive the product shown in pics 1-2, or pics 3-4, or something different.

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS UPDATE 11-30-2009: I initially gave this unit a rating of 3 stars. I am upgrading it to 4 stars because of a firmware upgrade that vastly improved the speed of the unit and eliminated issues I saw with VantagePoint. That said, I am leaving my original write-up intact.

---

I am an avid geocacher, and I have other hand-held units by Garmin and DeLorme. I have never used a Magellan GPS though I have friends who have used an Explorist for years with reasonable results. I was anxious to try out this unit to see if Magellan puts out a good product. In a nutshell, it is a mixed bag though overall the Triton 400 is a nice unit.

This is a very small unit, a little smaller than my Garmin eTrex Legend which is a fairly simple unit. Small is not necessarily a bad thing. It fits nicely in a pocket or a stash bag, being about the size of a cell phone.

The display is small too and people who want a large display will not like this unit. That said, the display is very bright, crisp and clear, everything being quite visible and readable. It had, in my opinion, the best general display of the units I have used, surpassing even the DeLorme in display quality.

Once the unit is powered on, it quickly starts finding satellites. Though it switches to navigation mode quickly, it is important to remember that the unit may or may not have a good lock on satellites - it may still be acquiring more. Be cautious in this regard, until used to using this unit.

The Triton has small buttons. I have big fingers. Surprisingly, this does not seem to be an issue, as I have not yet had the misfortune of mis-keying anything.

Several reviewers have complained that the menu system on the Triton is confusing, unintuitive and hard to use. I did not find this to be the case. I can simply say they are different than Garmin's implementations. That is neither good nor bad - just, different. Once used to them, this unit is no less intuitive than any other unit.

Navigation is straightforward and easy. When navigating I have found the unit to be on par with my Garmin GPSMap 60CSx, which is usually fairly accurate. I've no complaints in this regard.

My disappointment with the Triton mostly involve what's [not] in the box and the software that the computer uses to interact with it. There is a single CD in the box that includes PDF versions of the manual. There are no printed manuals in the box, at all. This is ok, but other units include a manual so it would be nice if this one did too. There is also a link to the website where you can download Vantage Point, the software for working with the unit. The software is 42MB, and I am on dial-up. Even including an older version would have been nice since there is plenty of room on the CD for it...

When the software is loaded on a Windows Vista machine, system behavior becomes very sluggish, mouse movement being choppy and COM port communications getting interruptions - enough interruptions to disconnect from the Internet. Though the software has eye appeal and offers a lot of functionality for dealing with the GPS, it drips of slowness. When sending caches to the unit, it sends at a rate of about 1 every 5-10 seconds, which means sending 500 at a time would take a good deal of time. That said, geocache information stops a little shy of being a paperless solution - the unit retains description, terrain/difficulty, owner and hint information, but it does not offer previous logs, sizes or other important bits of information. It's a good reference in the field but not sufficient to go true paperless.

Though there is a place on the bottom of the unit for a lanyard, it is disappointing that there is none in the box.

One area of real concern for me is the connection interface for the unit. The connector on the unit is exposed and uncovered, with nothing to keep it from getting dirty. If nothing else there should be a rubber flap over it, or a cover, or *something*.

This is actually a nice unit, with a decent feature set and good accuracy. Magellan cut some corners and left out some details that keep this from being a great unit. The technology is there. The design is there. The details are not. Hopefully Magellan will close the gap on these details soon.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS

Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown I've had several pairs of Sennheisers before the momentums namely a pair of HD580's from back in 1999 & much more recently a pair of HD650's. Let me start off by saying I'm not an "audiofile" I'm not a headphones snob. I don't name drop as to act like I know everything about all "cans" as they're referred to as. But I do know music & I know MY TYPE of music, which is pretty much everything except Country/Western. I listen 100% through my iphone or iPods.

I come from an LP, then 8 track (yuck), then cassette, then CD background so when I finally went all compressed format I didn't realize what I'd be "missing" I just thought, "Wow what a convenience"!! Anyway, I ended up ditching all my CD's (about 1400 total, originals!) & ripping them into iTunes, total of about 7500 songs. I long ago sold my HD580 back in 2005 & just listened from earbuds. I got tired of these real quick. So I saved up & did my research & just knew I had to have the Senn HD650's but I knew I had to have a good amp so I bought both (used) & I was thoroughly disappointed. I didn't hear this "wide open" expanded 3D imaged sound that everyone bragged about. After "damning" these headphones for being overpriced I realized, after my anger, I was being angry at the wrong item, it wasn't the can's it was the compressed format that removed all the subtle nuances of the original recordings!

So back to the drawing board to look for a decently priced (new) set of headphones. I bought a pair of in ear headphones from Sennhesier of course & these sounded good, better than than the Apple buds. Then I ran into the Momentums! I did my youtube & google research & the Momentums appear to be the one's I've been looking for. It has the controller but are "can" style headphones not earbuds! The cord is just long enough so i can stick my iphone in my pocket but no so long that it'll get caught on a doorknob or something else. The only drawback is it was hard to find the black with red from any type of discount. I got the brown ones reluctantly but I couldn't argue the price I got them for and for what it's worth the brown looks pretty clean & euro with the brushed aluminum.

I knew as soon as I started listening to some of the typical songs I play that I found my pair. They're paired perfectly for the portable MP3, phone or tablet's. You don't need an amp of any kind, they have great sound quality even for a sealed back design an because they're sealed you won't bother anyone sitting next to you at moderate levels. I was kind of put off of how small the ear surroundings were because my ears are not huge but they do stick out a bit, once I found a good position my ears fit fine.

All I can say is that I"m finally happy with a pair of headphones. I think the challenge is to match your style of music with headphones. Don't listen to name droppers & snobs who only talk about Gredo, AKG's HiFiMan & even Sennheisers. People knock Beats by Dre but hey if your music is like 99% current day hip hop & Dance then the Beats are probably the best suited for you. They're not for people who listen to live rock or classical. I had to find that out the hard way those higher priced headphones that require DAC's & AMPS aren't necessarily suited to my music. I believe the momentums are a great "in betweener" set of headphones. For that person who's aged a bit where they're not looking for LOUD & BOOM any more, they know & want detailed sound but they're still at a stage where they're listening to their music in a compressed 256k or less format, mp3 or wave format & not CD's anymore, but want that CD sound brought back.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown

text_fidelity_a:
Crucial Ballistix RGB 3200 MHz DDR4 DRAM Desktop Gaming Memory Kit 32GB (16GBx2) CL16 BL2K16G32C16U4BL (Black) These sticks are a hair faster than my previous DIMMs, which were also rated with a 3200mhz XMP profile. I actually really like the LEDs on them because I happen to have an MSI motherboard that recognized them instantly and let me control the lights via their Mystic Light setup. The glow adds a cool look to the case, and can also be used to keep an eye on CPU temp (you can have the colors change as the CPU temp rises). The ones I got were 16-18-18-36 timings, which actually were close enough to my G.Skill ram that I could combine them and get pretty good performance out of both kits together.
The only thing I didn't like, however, is how the height was difficult to work around my heat sync. I had to switch which DIMM slots I used because the one closest to my cooling system didn't have enough height clearance to fit. Thankfully my other RAM could slide in there and I now have these LED ones in the other 2 slots. So, just keep that in mind if you have a tight space and a large heat pipe system, you might need shorter DIMMs that forgo the LED.
I'm actually quite happy that I was able to make this work, there was a moment in which I was almost going to give up. If they'll fit in your setup, I'd say they are pretty cool looking and plenty fast for a modern Mobo.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial Ballistix RGB 3200 MHz DDR4 DRAM Desktop Gaming Memory Kit 32GB (16GBx2) CL16 BL2K16G32C16U4BL (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500) Compared to the Crucial 1TB M2 NVME I reviewed earlier, this Sabrent 512GB model benchmarks a little faster. And it works just fine on a PCI M2 adapter card, which are only a few bucks. (I bought the cheapest one available and it works.)

The NVME still offers much faster R/W speeds than other drives even when used with SATA 1 (as on my workstation). For example, the SSD I was using as my hard disk benchmarks at about 220MB/second. The Sabrent NVME on a PCI card benchmarks at about 1.5GB/second.

This time I experimented to see if I could get Debian Linux distro running on the NVME on my older workstation.

It took a few tries. Getting the OS to boot directly from the NVME was a no-go. Since the NVME is mounted on an adapter card, I had hoped it would trick the system into thinking it was just an ordinary SATA drive and boot from it. But that didn't happen.

So what I did was installed all the Linux OS EXCEPT for the boot folder on the NVME, and put the boot folder on the SSD HDD. So it boots from the SSD but the entire OS is on the NVME and runs from it.

Step one:

The partition manager in the Debian installer didn't want to partition the NVME at first.

So I bailed out of it and used GParted (Gnome disks utility couldn't do this) to "create partition table" and selected msdos as type. That wiped everything and turned the whole drive into unallocated space. From that point the partition manager worked.

Step two:

From the linux bootable USB installer I partitioned the SSD (not the NVME) with a primary partition labeled (to be mounted) as /boot. (You can make this partition most any size from a few GB on up---the boot files don't require a lot of space.) The remaining space I manually labeled as /msc.

I partitioned the NVME so the installer would put everything else on it, starting with / (root). You can simply make the whole NVME / root and the installer will take care of putting everything else on that drive, or you can do what I did and set up size-defined partitions for /home, /usr, and so on.

After installing the system, the installer asks where you want the bootloader GRUB installed. I selected the SSD.

It worked. The SSD does the booting to the NVME, which then runs the OS. And it did improve speed.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500)

That said, it does what it is supposed to do, it does it well and I am happy with it.

Setup is simple and easy. If you have your media ready to go, copy it to the included SD card and pop it in.

On a side note, the card that came with it is 32GB which is huge. That can hold literally thousands of full-resolution images from a digital camera. Assuming that the average high-resolution JPG image is 8mb (which is what comes off my mirrorless camera) it can hold about 4,000 pictures. That all said, this frame can also play back video and sound, so there is more to it than just showing pictures. In that light, the size of the card makes a lot of sense.

The frame is approximately 10” of viewing area. The images are bright and clear which should please most users.

The unit handles a number of audio, video and image formats. The list is not exhaustive, but it does handle the main types in each category.

Included is a little remote. The remote isn’t fancy but it is sufficient for changing settings, moving to the next media element, power on/off, etc.

There’s really only one negative, and that’s the documentation which is written in very poorly-translated English. I would lower my rating of the overall package on this basis except that the product is so self-explanatory and easy to use/understand that the documentation isn’t necessary.

Overall, we are happy with this frame. It works well and it is very easy and straightforward to understand. It handles a lot of formats and can play back audio and video in addition to showing still images.

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This camera is yet another product made in China and sold here in the United States for prices equivalent to what we'd pay if the thing was actually made in the USA, which IT IS NOT. The plastic it's made with seems cheap and brittle.

The setup instructions are WRONG and can lead you through a lengthy hell to install and configure the camera. The camera DID NOT HAVE THE MOST CURRENT SOFTWARE and I was forced through an update TWICE because the first one was the wrong one. Yes, the wrong one was recommended on their website. It took a second pass to get the correct version. Speaking of their website, it's a real mess, difficult to navigate, impossible to locate what you need on it, and just plain annoying. Tech support is mostly via email and the one time I did get a human, he didn't know much about anything.

You may want to use the camera's web interface to set up security and so forth. The GOTCHA is the cameras use Java and Java is going to drive your internet security software, firewall and virus protection wild. Java is known to be a welcome mat announcing your computer is open for all manner of malware, virus infections and so on. My security software blocked the install entirely.

Access to the camera remotely is via the D-Link website through an account you set up. To see the camera's video you must go to the website, log in and then view the camera. As video goes from camera to the D-Link website and then to you via your mobile device, the panning and zooming is jerky due to the lag in the up and download of the signal.

If you're looking for a security camera to use while traveling, or out for an evening, this will take care of things--barely. If you want a home security system with multiple cameras, go for a dedicated system with hard-wired cameras, a DVR and a solid wall around it for security. This camera is a toy compared to industrial or home-grade security.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
