PIONEER DV-610V-K MULTI REGION 1080p UPCONVERTING DVD PLAYER This is the most amazingly satisfying electronics product I have ever bought. The features are many and easy to learn. I especially enjoy some of the audio and video adjustment features:
Audio: DRC setting helps bring up quieter sounds while controlling loud peaks. Great for taming those annoying audio surges in 'background' music or battle scenes, etc. The Dialog feature lets you adjust the dialog perception so that you can hear the voices better over the background sounds in the soundtracks.
Video: You can adjust the Sharpness, Brightness, Contrast, Gamma, Hue, Chroma Level and BNR (block noise reduction). Each one has several levels to choose from and you get to sample it as it adjusts, so you can skip back and forth and compare the difference before you decide what to settle on.
The USB mode has great, easy to navigate menus. You can also record to your thumb drive from a CD that you are playing. There is a choice of different bit rates to do this and you can record individual tracks or all tracks. Very user-friendly menus for all these choices.
This unit has too many features to list, especially for someone like me, who is not quite fluent in tech terminology. Suffice it to say that it performs all the functions beautifully, the manual is very user-friendly and not only tells you how to adjust/change the various settings, but also explains the technical terminology in real English, so you know what those settings actually do when activated.
And if all that weren't enough, I scouted around a bit and bought the silver version (DV-610AV-S)of this unit for $30.00 less than the black one! (look for the one that ships for free with Amazon.com) Other than the color of the case, it is identical to the black one. I know, I looked them both up on Pioneer's web site and compared them point by point.
I do love the region-free feature too. But for me, this is more ho-hum, since I already owned one - a far inferior quality Philips one.
About the only thing I can think of to improve the user-friendliness of this product would be to have an alphabetized index in the manual. But, since it's only a 61 page manual, it's not such a big issue overall.
Another suggestion I would have would be to allow to record audio from DVDs also. So often, the audio track on a DVD sounds so much better than the soundtrack that is published on CD (i.e.: Brassed Off, Eyes Wide Shut), although I recognize there may be some copyright issues with that concept.
For the record: I am getting a second unit for my upstairs TV. Have I mentioned that I love it...? This is a really great product!!!
P.S.: Adding this comment on Jan. 17, 2010: I see the price difference between the black and the silver model is now up to $90.00!!! The silver one is the very same model, folks, but $ 90.00 cheaper!!! I am still just as enthused about this player as I was when I first reviewed it. I now own 2 units. Superb product!!!

ZEXMTE 6FT Optical Audio Cable, Fiber Optic Cable, 24K Gold-Plated Ultra-Durability Audio Cable, Slim Optical Cable Digital Audio Cable for Home Theater, Sound Bar, TV, PS4, Xbox I'm getting very great sounding, digital, Dolby sound through this cable. The right angle connection reduces the depth of the cable behind my receiver but it still sticks out further than I expected. The connectors clip into the ports pretty well, I have moved the receiver around a bunch since adding the cable & it hasn't pulled out. I ordered the 10' cord & needed all of it for my ceiling mounted television installation.
I have never used optical sound cables before but the receiver I picked up used did not have HDMI. My inexperience with these was readily apparent when I couldn't get the plugs to stay in the sockets on the components. I finally discovered that there are tiny, protective caps over the optical input/output.
The right angle connector doesn't fit quite as close as I imagined but it does make a difference in getting the cable behind my receiver on the shelf. The cable blocks whatever connections are below it but that wasn't an issue for my setup. That said, I don't understand why these connections have to be indexed at all if it is just the light going through the center it shouldn't matter what angle it comes in.
text_fidelity_b: ZEXMTE 6FT Optical Audio Cable, Fiber Optic Cable, 24K Gold-Plated Ultra-Durability Audio Cable, Slim Optical Cable Digital Audio Cable for Home Theater, Sound Bar, TV, PS4, Xbox

text_fidelity_a:
Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming I've had this camera a few months. The install went pretty well. I had to reboot a few times to pick the camera up, but once it was recognized, that has worked well. The camera does not clamp securely onto my external monitor. I fixed that problem by getting a separate flexible arm that clamps onto my desk and holds the camara. I love the physical lens cover so I can easily control when the camera is capturing an image. The picture quality is great. I love having an external camera instead of relying on the one on my laptop so my laptop can stay connected to the docking station and I don't have to try to get it moved over to the center of my desk every time I have a videoconference. Unfortnately there there are two remaining problems that are making me now decide to look for another camera:

1. Echos: When using this camera, is it causes an echo on videoconferencing that others can hear. I cannot hear it. It is so annoying to others that immediately people start talking about it and asking if the call can be done using some other audio. It definitely happens on Microsoft Teams calls as others have said in the Questions section for this product on Amazon. I can't remember if it happened on Webex videocalls also. Others have said switching the audio source solves that problem.

2. Wide View: This may be standard on these cameras. I'll find out when I shop for a new one, but the view is much wider than my native laptop camera. I can't find any way on the camera to "crop" it so that it shows only the person during videoconference and not a lot of what is to the right and left of the person. I solved that problem by installing OBS Studio and the OBS virtual camera. OBS allows me to crop the picture and then uses that video as the "camera" in Microsoft Teams. That works very well to get a good cropped video, however, the image quality went way down and it freezes up sometimes, so it is not a great solution because I end up not having smooth starts to videoconferences with all the troubleshooting I have to do to get OBS, the webcam, and the conferecing software to all work together.

I hope I can find a camera that works seemlessly so that the now much more frequent videoconferences, thanks to the pandemic, will go more smoothly.
text_fidelity_b: Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming

text_fidelity_a:
Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable I ordered the 'Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts and experiences.
First off, out of the box this Bluetooth Wireless Speaker not only looks interesting but it is beautiful. I say interesting because I have never had a Wireless Speaker like this, and I wonder where would I use it and would it be practical. Well after some time with this device I must first report that it really does sound amazing. The sound is clean and immersive. It is hard to describe the incredible sound sensation while wearing it. It is almost as if you have speakers floating on either side of your head (pointing directly to your ears) and it is nothing like I have experienced before but it is pretty cool. I have been trying to think of how this Speaker would actually fit into my life. It's not like you are wearing headphones that only you can hear. While wearing this speaker, everyone else around you can hear it too but it's just not as immersive as it is to you. It's hard to describe, but what I will say is that it really is an incredible experience. If the volume is down low you can still hear your surroundings yet when you crank it up, surprisingly your surrounding sounds seem to disappear. Personally I have decided that this would be best worn while alone in your home while doing simple household chores. Like doing dishes or folding laundry. The Nomodo U speaker stays put pretty well for the most part due to the rubber neck pad, yet if you are constantly bending over or doing anything where you are moving around a lot and twisting your head and body, it tends to need re adjusted. Sitting in bed listening to Music or listening to an audio book works really well with this device as long as you wont be disturbing your partner. As for watching movies, for me this really doesn't work. I can't find anywhere where it says what version of Bluetooth this is using but I don't think it is Bluetooth 5.0 unfortunately. There are noticeable sync issues and this just gets annoying. Speaking of the Bluetooth, it connects/pairs effortlessly to all of my devices and that is a bonus. I am disappointed however that it uses Micro USB (the cable is included btw) for charging. With this being a new device it should have USB Type C. I always have to mention this with any new devices. Call quality is acceptable. Those on the other end can hear you just fine, as long as you are not in a loud environment. This is pretty typical with most wireless headphones. Overall I do love this device and think it is a great value for what it is.
text_fidelity_b: Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable

Surge Protector Power Strip - Flat Plug Extension Cord, TROND 8 Widely-Spaced Outlets, 4 USB Charger(1 USB C Port), 5FT Ultra Thin Cord, 1440J, Flat Wall Plug, Desk Charging Station for Travel, White The TROND Flat Plug Power Strip Surge Protector is a great concept. Everything about it shows that some thought has been given to its design. Unfortunately, their choice of materials weren't as well thought out.

Some design concepts that attracted me to this surge protector is that it gives you 8 power plugs in a surface area that's just under 4 x 4 inches. The four plugs at the top are grounded while the 4 on the side are two-prongs. In addition, the wall plug is flat, giving you a lot of options as to where you can plug this product in. Finally, there are three USB-A ports and one USB-C port.

However, as I've mentioned, some design choices are questionable. As with many surge protectors, the USB ports are under-powered. The Type-A ports are not too bad at 5V/2.4A, but there is no quick charge capability. The Type-C is not PD, so your charging options are no better than the Type-A ports. You're stuck with 5V/3A with a total wattage shared between them at 14W or 3.4A.

My second gripe is with the build material. Compared to many power strips, the plastic covering this product feels quite cheap. It has a smooth texture and just feels... thin to the touch. The same plastic also covers the wall plug. In addition, the power wire is thinner than other power strips that you'll find. They feel more like the two-prong extension cords, except that it has three wires.

Now, I don't have proof that their choice of materials will be an issue at all, but it does give me pause.
text_fidelity_b: Surge Protector Power Strip - Flat Plug Extension Cord, TROND 8 Widely-Spaced Outlets, 4 USB Charger(1 USB C Port), 5FT Ultra Thin Cord, 1440J, Flat Wall Plug, Desk Charging Station for Travel, White

D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D) This will tell you if a battery is good or bad. However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.
text_fidelity_b: D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D)

My advise, and to save you some time: Do not get the app. It is so invasive of your information, and I know all apps are, but this one is probably the worst. You can set up bluetooth with all your devices without the app, and use all the features, no problem.

It also has Alexa built in, which is insane, I have yet to pull the trigger on giving Alexa permission, but I think I will; there is an Alexa button, I THINK that's the only time it's listening. If you're like me, and you have Amazon Prime Music the combo is insane.

A few cons: the Noise Cancellation will pound your ears if you’re not listening to content. I didn’t know it could do this, but I can see why people say they can only wear them for so long.

Do not under any circumstance get the app. It’s much more invasive than any app I’ve seen (of tkunborher to read the privacy (publicity) statement. Your earphones can operate fine without the app.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) I recently purchased this to replace a lost remote for a piece of high end integrated amp. As with most things in the audiophile world, a replacement for this simple 6 button remote was way overpriced ($105) for what it is. So I was pleased to find that my amplifier was supported by the Logitech 650.

My biggest gripe is nearly a dealbreaker. After setting it up I went to use it on my integrated amplifier to raise the volume a little bit. The problem was that I couldn't just give the volume button a quick tap to turn up the volume a little bit. A quick tap of the volume raised the volume a significant amount whereas the original amp controller allowed me to make volume changes in small increments. After some searching I found that I just had to adjust the IR repeat length in the controller setup.

Problem solved, right? Wrong.

First issue was the manual being outdated. The frustration started when I tried following the steps in the manual. The first step was "Click Troubleshoot at the top of the Harmony Remote Software window". The problem was that there was no Troubleshoot button anymore. They had updated the software but didn't update the manual. Eventually I found the new location in the software where you can lower the repeats. The default was set to 1 so I lowered it to 0 (the lowest setting on the 0-4 scale). I saved my changes and after waiting for the remote to update I tried it again and it still was making large volume changes. With the remote already set to the lowest setting the only way I can make small adjustments to volume is to press the volume button and cover the IR emitter on the remote extremely fast so the volume change signal only gets sent out for a quick burst. I'm talking ninja fast. This is extremely annoying and tricky to get the hang of.

PROS
-Price
-Device Compatibility

CONS
-Can't make small volume changes
-Outdated Manual (they updated the software but didn't update the PDF manual with new instructions for the new software). This causes some serious frustration when you are instructed in Step 1 to press a Troubleshooting button that no longer exists.

Final thoughts... I bought this to mainly do one thing. Change volume and input selection on my integrated amp. The inability to change the volume in small increments is a constant annoyance. It should be something that can be fixed with a software or firmware update.

Logitech, please fix this on the software/firmware side.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device

STEAMEMO 11-Port Ethernet Unmanaged PoE Switch, 8 PoE+ Ports@100W, 2 Gigabit Uplinks, 1*1.25G SFP Port, 250m Extend Mode, Fanless Sturdy Metal ,Plug and Play, Desktop or Wall Mount This powerful, silent, unmanaged Ethernet switch has 24 fast PoE ports (100 Mbps) that not only provide high speed internet (2 Gigabit Uplink) but automatically detects if the plugged in device needs power and, if so, how much!

I did thorough testing on this unit over the last several months and I am thoroughly impressed by the performance.

By utilizing the built in chip this switch will provide up to 30 watts to every Ethernet device connected (up to a total of 360 watts) but will not provide any power to devices that do not require power. I found that this switch works absolutely flawlessly.

Having the capability to provide ample internet speed and power at the same time makes this switch perfect for both business environments and as a hub for security systems.

I used this switch within my security system setup and mounted it within my security closet. I love that it is easily wall mountable but it can also be mounted within a rack with no problem.

I’ve tested my unit extensively using different security cameras and the results are nothing short of incredible. While most security cameras can be run via WiFi, nearly all of them still require a power adapter be plugged in. By utilizing this hub, security breaches are all but eliminated - by utilizing Ethernet instead of Wifi transmission your local storage unit makes it so there is no easy out of network access. In addition, transfer speed, resolution and picture quality is greatly increased - making the entire system more useful. In my experience, I found power is much easier to manage utilizing this method as opposed to having to run separate power supplies to each camera.

I have found this switch is rock solid and perfect for use as an unmanaged PoE switch for security cameras.

This is an all around outstanding product that I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend. This unit is sure to hold up well and perform even better.
